title: Radiant Royal Paisley Mehndi Design for Back Hand
descriptionParagraphs: An enchanting royal mehndi design tailored for the back of the hand, featuring mandala and circular medallion. Rated as Hard, this pattern is perfect for everyday.

Skin on the back of the hand is thinner than the palm, so the stain is usually lighter and fades sooner. Leaving the paste on for longer helps the colour develop. This pattern needs steady pressure control and fine line work, so it is best attempted after practising simpler designs.
The style uses dense coverage and is mainly chosen for bridal mehndi. Arched window frames, known as jharokha, are often used to frame the figures.
Application tips: The stain starts orange and darkens to reddish brown over 24 to 48 hours as it oxidises. Wash and dry the skin before application and skip lotion or oil, which block the dye.

image.alt: Royal Paisley mehndi design for back hand — radiant henna pattern

faq.q: How long does a mehndi stain last?
faq.a: A natural henna stain usually lasts one to three weeks. It fades faster on areas that are washed or rubbed often, such as the hands.

faq.q: How long should I leave the mehndi paste on?
faq.a: Keep the paste on for at least four to six hours. Many people leave it overnight for a darker stain.

faq.q: Why does my mehndi look orange at first?
faq.a: Fresh henna stains are orange. The colour deepens to reddish brown over the next 24 to 48 hours as the dye oxidises.

title: Gorgeous Royal Heart Vine Mehndi Design for Back Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A captivating royal mehndi design tailored for the back of the hand, featuring net pattern and wave pattern. Rated as Easy, this pattern is perfect for Eid.

Skin on the back of the hand is thinner than the palm, so the stain is usually lighter and fades sooner. Leaving the paste on for longer helps the colour develop. This is a beginner-friendly pattern: practise the main shapes on paper first, then copy them onto skin with a fine-tipped cone.

Royal mehndi draws on motifs from Mughal art and architecture, such as domes, arches and formal floral panels. Designs often show a bride and groom, a palanquin (doli) or elephants in a wedding procession.
Application tips: Keeping the skin warm while the paste is on helps the colour develop. Sketch the main figures first and build the borders around them.

image.alt: Royal Heart Vine mehndi design for back hand — gorgeous henna pattern

faq.q: How long should I leave the mehndi paste on?
faq.a: Keep the paste on for at least four to six hours. Many people leave it overnight for a darker stain.

faq.q: Why does my mehndi look orange at first?
faq.a: Fresh henna stains are orange. The colour deepens to reddish brown over the next 24 to 48 hours as the dye oxidises.

faq.q: Is black henna safe?
faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

title: Radiant Royal Chain Link Mehndi Design for Foot
descriptionParagraphs: An elegant royal mehndi design tailored for the foot, featuring spiral rosette and bell garland. Rated as Expert, this pattern is perfect for Karva Chauth.

The soles take henna as well as the palms do, while the top of the foot stains lighter. Stay seated and avoid walking until the paste has dried completely. This is a detailed pattern usually done by an experienced artist; allow plenty of time and work in small sections.
The style uses dense coverage and is mainly chosen for bridal mehndi. Arched window frames, known as jharokha, are often used to frame the figures.
Application tips: Book an experienced artist for portrait work; faces are the hardest part of this style. Allow several hours for both hands and feet.

image.alt: Royal Chain Link mehndi design for foot — radiant henna pattern

faq.q: Why does my mehndi look orange at first?
faq.a: Fresh henna stains are orange. The colour deepens to reddish brown over the next 24 to 48 hours as the dye oxidises.

faq.q: Is black henna safe?
faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

faq.q: How can I make my mehndi darker?
faq.a: Leave the paste on longer, seal it with lemon and sugar, keep the skin warm, and avoid water for the first day after removing the paste.

title: Dainty Royal Lotus Pattern Mehndi Design for Full Hand
descriptionParagraphs: An elegant royal mehndi design providing full hand coverage, featuring ring pattern and heart vine. Rated as Medium, this pattern is perfect for an engagement.

Full-hand designs run from the fingertips to the wrist, so allow extra time for application. Work from the wrist towards the fingers, or the other way round, so you never rest on wet paste. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.

Royal mehndi draws on motifs from Mughal art and architecture, such as domes, arches and formal floral panels. Designs often show a bride and groom, a palanquin (doli) or elephants in a wedding procession.

Application tips: Leave the paste on for at least four to six hours; the longer it stays, the deeper the stain. Dab a lemon and sugar mixture on the dried paste to keep it moist and stuck to the skin.

image.alt: Royal Lotus Pattern mehndi design for full hand — dainty henna pattern

faq.q: Is black henna safe?
faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

faq.q: How can I make my mehndi darker?
faq.a: Leave the paste on longer, seal it with lemon and sugar, keep the skin warm, and avoid water for the first day after removing the paste.

faq.q: Should I do a patch test before applying mehndi?
faq.a: Yes. Apply a small amount of the paste to the inner arm and wait 24 hours, especially if you have sensitive skin or are using a new cone.

title: Stunning Royal Dotwork Mehndi Design for Finger
descriptionParagraphs: An elaborate royal mehndi design designed for the fingers, featuring chain link and feather stroke. Rated as Hard, this pattern is perfect for a party.

Finger designs are quick to apply and dry fast, which makes them practical when time is short. Fingertips have thicker skin, so the stain there usually develops darker than on the rest of the hand. This pattern needs steady pressure control and fine line work, so it is best attempted after practising simpler designs.
The style uses dense coverage and is mainly chosen for bridal mehndi. Arched window frames, known as jharokha, are often used to frame the figures.

Application tips: Scrape the dried paste off instead of washing it, and keep the area away from water for the first 12 to 24 hours. The stain starts orange and darkens to reddish brown over 24 to 48 hours as it oxidises.
